title: Effective descent in the affine flat surjective case
statement: Let $X$ and $S$ be affine schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:X\to S$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Let $V\to X$ be an affine morphism [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and let $D$ be a descent datum on $V$ relative to $X/S$ [def-pd-descent-datum]. Then $D$ is effective: there are a scheme $U\to S$ and a morphism $q:V\to U$ which exhibit $V$ as the fibre product $U\times_S X$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and $q$ is invariant under the transport of $D$.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 0245 (lemma-affine), proof, affine flat surjective case; Steps 3-7 of lem-galois-fpqc-affine-descent-effective.

proof.text: Step 1 (affine coordinates and universal transport). Since V -> X is affine and X is affine, V is affine [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. Use R = Gamma(S), A = Gamma(X), E = Gamma(V), with the algebra structures induced by the structure maps [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-scheme]. The scalar tower is given by functoriality of global sections. Flatness of f gives Module.Flat R A [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine]. Let P = V times_S X [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections pr1 and pr2. Evaluate D's transport [def-pd-descent-datum] at the universal pair pr1 followed by V -> X, and pr2, to obtain gamma : P -> V with gamma followed by V -> X equal to pr2. Naturality identifies g followed by gamma with transport of the point g followed by pr1 for every g : T -> P.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0245, proof: 'Say X = Spec(A) and S = Spec(R) so that R -> A is a faithfully flat ring map ... V = Spec(B) for some A-algebra B (Morphisms, Definition 01S6)'

proof.text: Step 2 (the coaction on coordinate rings). The affine tensor-product identification [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra, lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] gives xi : A tensor_R E isomorphic to Gamma(P), with xi(a tensor e) = pr2^*(a) pr1^*(e). In Lean, use the proved source-library isPushout_appTop_of_flat and IsPushout.tensorEquiv to realize this identification. Define delta = xi^{-1} composed with gamma^*. Since gamma is over pr2, delta is an A-algebra homomorphism E -> A tensor_R E [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Lemma Tag 0245, proof: 'The isomorphism phi corresponds to an isomorphism of rings phi^#: B (x)_R A <- A (x)_R B as A (x)_R A-algebras. The cocycle condition ... Inverting these arrows ... descent datum for modules ... Definition 023G' (definition-descent-datum-modules, line 271)

proof.text: Step 3 (counit and coassociativity). The diagonal d : V -> P, with projections identity and V -> X, satisfies d followed by gamma = identity: apply naturality and transport_self of [def-pd-descent-datum]. On pure tensors this says d^* composed with xi is the multiplication map, so delta is counital. For P2 = P times_S X, form gamma1 and pi1 : P2 -> P with first projections r1 followed respectively by gamma and pr1, and common second projection r2. Naturality and transport_transport give gamma1 followed by gamma = pi1 followed by gamma. Identify Gamma(P2) with A tensor_R Gamma(P), then with A tensor_R (A tensor_R E) using [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Tensor induction shows that gamma1^* is id tensor delta and pi1^* is id tensor includeRight under these identifications. The preceding geometric cocycle is exactly the coassociativity identity.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0245, proof (the cocycle diagram, lines 9180-9188); Definition Tag 023V and the paragraph after it (line 8136: 'In fact, Delta^* phi is equal to the identity. This is a good exercise'), written out here

proof.text: Step 4 (algebra descent). The coaction and the two laws form Algebra.DescentDatum R A E. Flat algebra descent [lem-galois-flat-algebra-descent] supplies C = {e in E : delta(e) = 1 tensor e} and the A-algebra isomorphism epsilon : A tensor_R C -> E, a tensor c |-> a*c, namely descendedEquiv. Use this isomorphism to transport the canonical tensor-product pushout to the square with vertices R, A, C, E [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property].

source.place: Lemma Tag 0245, proof, lines 9192-9200 (Proposition Tag 023N, proposition-descent-module)

proof.text: Step 5 (spectrum and transport compatibility). Apply Spec to the pushout square [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Paste with the natural affine isomorphisms X isomorphic to Spec Gamma(X), S isomorphic to Spec Gamma(S), and V isomorphic to Spec Gamma(V) [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-fibre-product]. This gives an actual pullback square with U = Spec C over S and q : V -> U induced by C -> E. To prove gamma followed by q = pr1 followed by q, apply the naturality of V -> Spec Gamma(V) and the faithfulness of Spec; on each c in C the ring-map equality is xi(delta(c)) = xi(1 tensor c) = pr1^*(c). For arbitrary points f1,f2 : T -> X and a : T -> V over f1, let g : T -> P have projections a and f2. Naturality identifies g followed by gamma with D.transport(f1,f2)(a). Precomposing the preceding equality with g proves the transport invariance required by IsEffective [def-pd-descent-datum].
